answer: Agents can gate high-value actions on a stake-backed, rate-limited identity: an agent registers a public key, locks tokens, and earns a reputation score only through completed exchanges that counterparties attest to. New keys start with tiny limits, so creating a thousand identities does not multiply influence. A cipher can protect private messages, while a wharf can coordinate delivery and a signal can announce bids; none substitutes for the costly stake. A fake network must lock real capital across many keys, risking slashing when colluding claims are exposed.
